name: Japanese Ink / Sumi-e
description: Monochrome ink painting: a few decisive brush strokes with tonal wash, generous empty paper (ma), and suggestion over description; energy (qi) lives in the stroke itself.
visual_characteristics: black ink in 4-5 tones (dry, grey, wash, wet-black) on warm rice paper
each stroke is a single gesture: thick-to-thin, dry-brush breaks, ink pooling
vast negative space; the subject occupies <= 40% and fades into mist
one red seal (hanko) and optionally a short calligraphic line as the only colour accent

palette.guidance: Paper #f3ecdc-ish, ink ramp from #111 to #d9d4c7 (4-5 tones), single vermilion seal #c1272d (<=1% of area). No other colours.

geometry: Organic brush-stroke shapes drawn as filled variable-width paths (not uniform strokes); bamboo nodes as short horizontal breaks; mountains as layered soft masses; asymmetric triangle balance.
stroke: Brush = closed path with tapered ends and irregular width; dry-brush = the same shape masked with streaky texture; hair-thin lines for grass/needles using 0.6-1.2 unit strokes with round caps.
texture: Rice-paper fibres (very faint feTurbulence), dry-brush bristle streaks (mask of thin horizontal lines with random gaps), wet-edge halo on washes (radial or blurred outer copy).
composition: Asymmetric, high or low placement; diagonal from lower-left to upper-right; one main mass + 1-2 accents; empty area is 60%+; seal in the lower corner balancing the mass.
typography: Brush calligraphy as shapes (or a single vertical line of Chinese/Japanese characters if the user supplies text); seal as a red square with knocked-out mark.
lighting_depth: No cast light; depth by tone (dark near, pale far), overlap and mist bands (semi-transparent paper-coloured gradients).
svg_techniques: washes: shapes with linearGradient/radialGradient in ink tones and one feGaussianBlur (stdDev 4-8) on a copy for the wet halo
dry brush: apply a <mask> containing a <pattern> of irregular thin lines to a stroke shape
mist = paper-coloured gradient bands with fill-opacity .5-.8 between layers
seal: <rect rx=2> vermilion + a knocked-out mark via evenodd or mask; slightly rotated
avoid: colour palettes beyond ink + one seal

name: Ukiyo-e
description: Japanese woodblock print language: flat colour regions separated by a confident key-block outline, limited pigment palette, bokashi gradations in skies, decorative patterning and traditional composition with cropped foregrounds.
visual_characteristics: flat colour blocks, each printed as a separate 'block' with slight registration offsets
organic, calligraphic key-block outlines of varying weight (thicker on outer contours)
limited pigment palette: indigo/Prussian blue, vermilion, ochre, sap green, warm cream paper, sumi black
decorative patterning for water (seigaiha, wave curls), clothing (kimono motifs), clouds (stylised bands), and grain-like wood texture in large areas
bokashi (graded wash) only at horizons/skies; everything else flat

palette.guidance: Paper #efe3c8. Prussian blue #1f3c6e (dominant), pale indigo #6d8fb3, vermilion #c8372d, ochre #d9a441, muted green #6b8f5a, sumi #1c1a19. Colours are slightly desaturated and warm-toned; 8-12 colours total.

geometry: Flattened perspective (no vanishing point; stacked planes), stylised waves as curling claw-like crests, clouds as banded ribbons, figures simplified with elegant curved contours; strong diagonals and cropping by frame.
stroke: Key-block outline in sumi: variable weight simulated by two stroke layers (3 units for exterior contour, 1-1.4 for interior detail); round caps, round joins; slight irregularity.
texture: Wood-grain: faint horizontal streak pattern (feTurbulence stretched baseFrequency 0.002 0.2, opacity ~6%) over colour blocks; paper fibre; slight mis-registration offset (0.6-1.2 units) between colour and key-line.
composition: Asymmetric traditional layout: large foreground element cropped at one edge (wave or branch), subject in the middle distance, Fuji/horizon high, decorative cartouche (title box) in a top corner with a red seal.
typography: Vertical title cartouche: rectangle with light fill and dark border, with text as brush-like shapes (or a simple vertical text placeholder in a serif generic font); small red artist seal.
lighting_depth: No cast shadows; depth by overlap, colour value (darker foreground), and bokashi mist bands.
svg_techniques: colour blocks first (no outlines), then a separate <g id="key-block"> of outline paths on top with slight translate(.8,.6) offset for mis-registration
seigaiha/wave pattern as a <pattern> of overlapping concentric arcs (3-4 rings) reused for water and sky bands
bokashi with a single vertical linearGradient limited to the sky region via clip-path
wood-grain overlay = one rect with feTurbulence stretched horizontally, low opacity, clipped to the picture area
seal = small vermilion rounded rect with knocked-out mark
avoid: just recolouring a generic drawing with 'Japanese' colours
